capabilities.description: Forwards each profile's Silo notifications to Pushover, and playback, watchdog and failure alerts to admins who turn them on.

Checks Silo's stream nodes, restart state, database and Redis, and the server's disk and memory, and sends a Pushover alert (and a recovery alert) to admins who turned it on. Needs the read-only Silo key. Suggested schedule: every 5 minutes.

Sends admins who turned it on a Pushover summary of the last 7 days: plays, time watched, top viewers and top titles. Each admin picks their own day and hour (default Sunday 18:00, in their time zone) and a run sends it in that hour or in any later run within 6 hours after (so a week isn't lost if Silo was down), at most once a week, so schedule it to run every hour. Needs the read-only Silo key. Suggested schedule: every 1 hour.

global_config_schema.title: Pushover
global_config_schema.description: Server-wide settings. Each profile adds its own Pushover user key from Apps > Pushover.

fields.label: Shared Pushover application token (optional)
fields.description: Used for profiles that don't enter their own application token. Leave blank to require every profile to bring its own. Pushover limits each application to 10,000 messages a month.

fields.label: Public URL override (optional)
fields.description: Base URL for "Open in Silo" links. Defaults to the server's configured public URL.

fields.label: Read-only Silo key (admin:monitor:read)
fields.description: Optional. An API key created on an admin account with only the admin:monitor:read scope. With it, each account's primary profile can set up Pushover for every profile on the account. Without it, each profile sets up its own. "Set up the read-only key" on the Pushover page fills this in for you. Don't use a full-access key.

fields.label: Session control key (admin:sessions:control)
fields.description: Optional. An API key created on an admin account with the admin:sessions:control scope, for the stop-stream page (Apps > Pushover, admin section, "Live streams"). It can be the same key as above if that key has both scopes. "Set up the read-only key" with "Also allow stopping streams" ticked fills this in for you.

sections.title: Silo API keys (optional)
sections.description: Scoped keys let the plugin read from Silo without full admin access. Silo's API Keys page creates only full-access keys, so the easiest way to get these is to open Apps > Pushover as an admin and use "Set up the read-only key": paste a full-access key once and the plugin creates the scoped keys, saves them here and can revoke the full-access key.

presentation.summary: Send each profile's Silo notifications to Pushover, with admin alerts for streams, watchdog checks and server health.
presentation.description_markdown:
Sends Silo's notifications to Pushover, and gives server admins Tautulli-style alerts.

**For every profile:** new episodes and request updates (approved, declined, fulfilled) go to the profile's own Pushover account, with its own device, sound, priority and wording. A profile can limit new-episode pushes to chosen reasons, merge a season drop into one push, and set quiet hours.

**For admins (each admin opts in on their own Pushover page):** who started, paused, resumed or stopped a stream, and what, how and on which device, with an optional poster and an "Open in Silo" link to Admin > Activity; playback failures; too many streams (per user or server-wide); bandwidth over a limit; a new device or IP address; failed scans and jobs; a server health check with a recovery message; and a weekly digest. Admins can filter by user, remote streams, transcodes, library or media type, pick a noise mode (collapse binges, per-user cooldown, every event), set quiet hours, make any alert an emergency that repeats until acknowledged, and edit the wording. A "Live streams" page lets an admin stop a stream, with or without a message.

Admin alerts need a **read-only Silo key** (`admin:monitor:read`). Stopping streams also needs a **session control key** (`admin:sessions:control`). Neither is a full-access key, and both are set up from the Pushover page.
presentation.setup_markdown:
1. Optionally register an application at https://pushover.net/apps and paste its token into **Shared Pushover application token**. Without one, each profile must enter its own. Pushover limits an application to 10,000 messages a month, so a busy server may want each admin to use their own token.
2. Each profile opens **Apps > Pushover**, adds their Pushover user key and chooses which notifications to receive.
3. **Silo keys (admins).** Silo's API Keys page can only make full-access keys, so the plugin makes the scoped ones for you. Create a full-access key under **Admin > API Keys**, open **Apps > Pushover** as an admin and paste it into **Set up the read-only key**. The plugin uses it once to create a key that can only read (`admin:monitor:read`), saves it, and, with **Delete this key from Silo** ticked (the default), revokes the one you pasted. Tick **Also allow stopping streams** to create a second key with `admin:sessions:control` for the **Live streams** page (Stop and Stop with message). The two key fields in this plugin's admin settings also accept keys you made yourself.
4. **Admin alerts.** Once the read-only key is saved, each admin opens **Apps > Pushover** and turns on the alerts they want, using their own profile's Pushover key. Alerts stop if the read-only key is revoked, and an account that is no longer an admin stops receiving them.
5. **Scheduled alerts** (server health check and weekly digest). Silo runs a plugin's scheduled task only on a schedule you give it, and a binding change needs a Silo restart. Open **Admin > Plugins**, open Pushover Notifications and bind the tasks, or call `PUT /api/v2/admin/plugins/installations/{id}/task-bindings/{capability_id}` with an admin API key. For `health_check` use an interval trigger of 5 minutes: `{"enabled": true, "trigger": {"type": "interval", "interval_ms": 300000}}`. For `weekly_digest` use an interval trigger of 1 hour, not a weekly one: `{"enabled": true, "trigger": {"type": "interval", "interval_ms": 3600000}}`. Each admin picks their digest day and hour (default Sunday 18:00, in their own time zone) on **Apps > Pushover**, and a run sends it in that hour or in any run up to 6 hours after, at most once a week. **Restart Silo after changing a binding.** Until a task is bound, Silo runs it once each time it starts.

Upgrading from 0.2.0: the full-access key it asked for is no longer used. Open **Apps > Pushover** as an admin and click **Replace the old full-access key**: the plugin uses it once to create the read-only key, then revokes it.
